metadata.note: The historical rail line connecting Charleston and Columbia, South Carolina. This is the Columbia Branch of the South Carolina Canal and Railroad Company, which split off the company's original Charleston-Hamburg main line (completed 1833, at the time the longest railroad in the world under single management) at Branchville. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap active-rail geometry for the rural middle stretch (Summerville to Hopkins, via Branchville, Orangeburg, and St. Matthews -- the real historic route, still active track). The two short endpoint approaches (Charleston terminal, and Hopkins into Columbia) could NOT be matched to a connected OSM rail path -- both are straight-line approximations to the city center, flagged honestly rather than guessed at closer precision.
sources: https://www.scencyclopedia.org/sce/entries/south-carolina-railroad/ (Charleston-Summerville-Branchville-Blackville-Aiken-Hamburg main line; consolidated into Southern Railway-Carolina Division in 1902)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Canal_and_Railroad_Company (chartered Dec 19 1827; Charleston-Hamburg main line completed October 1833, 136 miles, first scheduled steam passenger service in the US; Columbia Branch built 1840, opened 1842, 66.3 miles from Branchville via Orangeburg-St.Matthews-Hopkins; 1844 merger with the Louisville, Cincinnati and Charleston RR formed the South Carolina Railroad Company)
https://schistory.org/june1842-the-locomotive-robert-y-hayne-travels-from-charleston-to-columbia/ (first train Charleston-Columbia arrived June 20 1842, locomotive Robert Y. Hayne)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era; precise route mileage/station list within the Charleston-Summerville-Branchville stretch; whether/when this route carried named passenger trains under Southern Railway (post-1902) or successor operators.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
